comments.author: Curious
comments.body: Just as a reminder to the noobies out there, this skill does NOT work when trying to read books at the Archives. If you are an adventurer, you'll need the actual language skills or get an aide(s) that have them. Translation notes also work for reading in the Archives but there are currently no translation notes available for Chinese and Japanese languages and the only aides that have those languages (as of right now) are Astro aides.

comments.author: ThatOneGuy
comments.body: You should carry plenty of vigor food to help keep from running out while using this skill, too! Though even if you did hit zero vigor, and had nobody around willing to help, I think all the player languages are spoken over at the Ganador camp, so you could always hop on the Special Transport Ship and refill at the bar there, in an emergency!

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
This skill will be adjusted in a fairly distant future "Atlantis - Atlantic Ocean" update (due out October 2015 in Japan; unknown date for GAMA). If I'm reading it correctly, then...

"Body Language will become favored by Adventure/Merchant/Maritime Mentor job classes. Its cost to use will apparently be reduced to 5 vigour per use."

That should make it a lot easier to get Body Language to R15 for skill refinement, itself a future option that gives the following bonus: "After a successful invocation in the city, it will not fail to leave the town".

So... use it once in town, and it'll succeed every time afterward until you leave that same town, I guess? Time will tell.

Source: gamecity.ne.jp/dol/developer/new_updata2015_10.htm (update info), gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?Skill/List (skill refinement info)

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
A trick for grinding this that I've used: go to a tavern or rest house where a Well-Dressed Gentleman NPC is (usually a "capital" port like Seville, Stockholm, Santo Domingo, etc.). You can click on "Talk to" with the WDG repeatedly with Body Language; there's no menu prompt to close/exit, meaning you can just keep on clicking "Talk to" until you're low on vigour... at which point, you can just turn around and refill at the nearby Barkeep.

There are probably other ways, probably even better ones, but that trick's served me well over the years. Cheers, and good skill grinding to you, however you go about it.
